hero_subtitle: AI-Powered Crop Disease Detection for Smart Farming
upload_desc: Take a clear photo of the affected leaf and upload it for instant AI analysis
upload_drag: Drag & drop your leaf image here
disease_healthy_desc: No signs of disease. The leaf appears normal and healthy with good color and texture.
disease_leaf_spot_desc: Circular dark spots on leaves caused by Cercospora fungus. Can reduce yield by 50% if untreated.
disease_rust_desc: Orange-brown pustules on leaf undersides caused by Puccinia arachidis. Spreads rapidly in humid conditions.
disease_alternaria_desc: Irregular brown lesions with concentric rings. Caused by Alternaria alternata in warm, humid weather.
disease_rosette_desc: Viral disease transmitted by aphids causing severe stunting, yellowing, and curling of leaves.
disease_potato_healthy_desc: No signs of disease. The potato plant appears normal with healthy foliage and growth.
disease_potato_bacteria_desc: Caused by Ralstonia solanacearum. Plants wilt rapidly even with adequate soil moisture.
disease_potato_fungi_desc: Caused by Alternaria solani. Dark concentric spots on older leaves leading to defoliation.
disease_potato_nematode_desc: Microscopic worms feeding on roots causing stunted growth, yellowing, and yield loss.
disease_potato_pest_desc: Insects like Colorado Potato Beetle feeding on foliage, causing defoliation and yield loss.
disease_potato_phytopthora_desc: Devastating disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. Can destroy a crop in days under cool, wet conditions.
disease_potato_virus_desc: Viral diseases transmitted by aphids causing mosaic patterns, leaf rolling, and stunted growth.
disease_pepper_healthy_desc: The pepper plant appears healthy with no signs of disease. Vibrant green leaves and normal growth.
disease_pepper_bacterial_desc: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris. Water-soaked spots on leaves that enlarge and turn brown with yellow halos.
disease_tomato_healthy_desc: The tomato plant appears healthy with vibrant green foliage and no signs of disease.
disease_tomato_bacterial_desc: Small, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves and fruit caused by Xanthomonas species.
disease_tomato_early_blight_desc: Concentric dark ring spots (target pattern) on older leaves caused by Alternaria solani.
disease_tomato_late_blight_desc: Devastating disease by Phytophthora infestans. Water-soaked lesions with white fuzzy mold underneath.
disease_tomato_leaf_mold_desc: Yellow spots on upper surface with olive-green velvety mold underneath. Common in greenhouses.
disease_tomato_septoria_desc: Numerous small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers. Tiny black dots visible in spot centers.
disease_tomato_spider_mite_desc: Fine stippling and webbing on leaves caused by two-spotted spider mites in hot, dry conditions.
disease_tomato_target_spot_desc: Brown spots with concentric ring patterns on leaves, stems, and fruit by Corynespora cassiicola.
disease_tomato_ylcv_desc: Devastating viral disease causing upward leaf curling, yellowing, and severe stunting. Spread by whiteflies.
disease_tomato_mosaic_desc: Highly contagious virus causing light/dark green mosaic patterns, leaf distortion, and stunted growth.
how_step1_desc: Take a clear photo of the affected leaf using your phone camera or upload an existing image.
how_step2_desc: Our AI model powered by MobileNetV2 analyzes the leaf image and identifies any diseases.
how_step3_desc: Receive instant treatment suggestions and prevention tips in your preferred language.
footer_desc: AI-powered crop disease detection for smarter, healthier farming.
toast_invalid_type: Invalid file type. Please upload an image (JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF).
toast_file_too_large: File too large. Maximum size is 16MB.
history_desc: View your past predictions and results
history_empty: No predictions yet. Upload a leaf image to get started!
healthy_causes_1: The leaf is in good health with no visible symptoms.
healthy_causes_2: Proper nutrition and watering are maintaining plant vigor.
healthy_treatment_1: No treatment needed — continue regular care.
healthy_treatment_3: Keep monitoring for early signs of disease.
healthy_prevention_3: Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation.
healthy_prevention_4: Apply preventive fungicide spray during rainy season.
leaf_spot_causes_2: Spreads through wind-borne spores and rain splash.
leaf_spot_treatment_3: Spray at 10-15 day intervals during disease progression.
leaf_spot_treatment_4: Remove and destroy severely infected leaves.
leaf_spot_prevention_2: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops.
leaf_spot_prevention_3: Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness.
leaf_spot_prevention_4: Apply preventive fungicide spray at 30-35 days after sowing.
rust_causes_3: Thrives in high humidity (>80%) and temperatures 20-28°C.
rust_treatment_1: Apply Triadimefon (1 g/L) or Hexaconazole (2 mL/L).
rust_treatment_3: Spray at first sign of pustules, repeat after 15 days.
rust_treatment_4: Combine contact and systemic fungicides for better control.
rust_prevention_2: Avoid late sowing — plant at recommended time.
rust_prevention_3: Remove volunteer groundnut plants from previous seasons.
rust_prevention_4: Maintain proper field drainage to reduce humidity.
alternaria_causes_2: Favored by warm, humid conditions and poor air circulation.
alternaria_causes_3: Spreads through infected seed and crop debris.
alternaria_treatment_3: Treat seeds with Thiram or Carbendazim before planting.
alternaria_treatment_4: Remove infected plant debris from the field.

Alternaria_Leaf_Spot.description: Caused by the fungus Alternaria alternata. Irregular brown lesions with concentric rings appear on leaves. It survives in crop debris.
symptoms: Leaves drying up and dropping off
causes: Caused by the fungus Alternaria alternata in warm, humid conditions.
treatment: Remove and burn infected plant parts
Apply fungicide within 48 hours of symptoms

Healthy.description: The plant appears healthy with no signs of disease.
causes: Optimal growing conditions and absence of pathogens.

Leaf_Spot_Early_and_Late.description: Caused by Cercospora arachidicola (early) and Cercosporidium personatum (late). Brown or black spots appear on leaves.
symptoms: Brown or dark spots on upper leaf surface
causes: Fungal infection thriving in warm, humid conditions.

Rosette.description: A viral disease transmitted by aphids. Causes severe stunting of plants and yellowing of leaves.
causes: Viral infection transmitted by the groundnut aphid.

Rust.description: Caused by the fungus Puccinia arachidis. Orange-brown pustules appear on the underside of leaves.
symptoms: Leaves turn brown and dry up
causes: Fungus Puccinia arachidis spreading via airborne spores.
treatment: Spray at first sign of pustules

Bacteria.description: Caused by Ralstonia solanacearum. Plants wilt rapidly even with adequate soil moisture.
symptoms: Rapid wilting of leaves and stems
Stems may show brown discoloration inside
White bacterial ooze from cut stems
causes: Bacterial infection through roots or wounded plant parts.

Fungi.description: Caused by Alternaria solani. Dark, concentric spots appear on older leaves first.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings
causes: Fungus spreading in warm, moist environments.

Nematode.description: Microscopic worms that feed on potato roots, causing poor growth and yield loss.
causes: Infestation of Globodera species in the soil.
prevention: Clean equipment to prevent soil spread

Pest.description: Insects feeding on potato foliage, which can completely defoliate the plant.
symptoms: Presence of larvae or adult beetles
causes: Insect pests multiplying rapidly in favorable conditions.
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak pest populations

Phytopthora.description: A devastating disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. Can destroy a crop in days under cool, wet conditions.
symptoms: Water-soaked, dark green spots on leaves
White fungal growth on leaf underside
causes: Oomycete pathogen thriving in cool, wet weather.

Virus.description: Viral diseases transmitted by aphids, causing mosaic patterns or leaf rolling.
symptoms: Mottled or mosaic patterns on leaves
causes: Viruses transmitted by aphid vectors or infected seed tubers.
treatment: Apply mineral oils to reduce transmission

Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris. Water-soaked spots appear on leaves, stems, and fruit.
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots enlarge and turn brown with yellow halo
causes: Bacterial infection (Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria) spread by rain splash and contaminated seeds.

Pepper__bell___healthy.description: The pepper plant appears healthy with no signs of disease.
causes: Optimal growing conditions and absence of pathogens.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas species. Small, dark, water-soaked lesions appear on leaves and fruit.
causes: Bacterial infection spread by rain splash, overhead irrigation, and contaminated seeds.

Tomato_Early_blight.description: Caused by Alternaria solani. Concentric dark rings (target spots) form on older leaves first.
symptoms: Dark concentric ring spots on lower leaves
causes: Fungus Alternaria solani thriving in warm, humid conditions with heavy dew.
treatment: Apply fungicide every 7-10 days in wet weather

Tomato_Late_blight.description: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Can devastate entire crops rapidly in cool, wet conditions.
symptoms: White fuzzy mold on leaf undersides
Dark brown firm rot on fruit
causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans favored by cool (15-22°C), wet weather.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.description: Caused by Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum). Mainly affects greenhouse tomatoes.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mold on underside
causes: Fungus Passalora fulva thriving in high humidity (>85%) and moderate temperatures.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Caused by Septoria lycopersici. Small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers.
symptoms: Dark brown borders with gray/tan centers
Tiny black dots (pycnidia) in spot centers
causes: Fungus Septoria lycopersici spread by rain splash and overhead irrigation.
treatment: Spray at first sign of disease

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.description: Caused by Tetranychus urticae. Tiny mites feed on leaf cells causing stippling and webbing.
causes: Infestation by two-spotted spider mites, favored by hot, dry conditions.
treatment: Spray with strong water jet to dislodge mites
Apply insecticidal soap or neem oil

Tomato__Target_Spot.description: Caused by Corynespora cassiicola. Concentric ring patterns appear on leaves, stems, and fruit.
symptoms: Small brown spots with concentric rings
causes: Fungus Corynespora cassiicola thriving in warm, humid environments.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.description: A devastating viral disease transmitted by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaves
Flower drop and reduced fruit set
causes: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus transmitted by silverleaf whitefly vectors.
treatment: No cure once infected — remove plants
Use yellow sticky traps for monitoring
Apply neem oil to reduce whitefly populations

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A highly contagious virus that causes mottled patterns and distorted growth.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves
causes: Tomato Mosaic Virus spread mechanically through contaminated tools, hands, and seeds.
treatment: Do not smoke near plants (tobacco mosaic cross-infection)

Tomato_healthy.description: The tomato plant appears healthy with no signs of disease or pest damage.
causes: Optimal growing conditions and absence of pathogens.
prevention: Monitor for early signs of disease
